Alliance

Data period: 2024 election manifesto and analysis. Published 2024. Source updated not supplied. Published 2024-01-31. Source updated not supplied.

This is a fixed past snapshot. No next release date is announced.

Selected official offer
End the two-child limit on benefits.
Party source excerpt
We support ending the Benefits Cap, Bedroom Tax and two-child limit on Child Benefit on a UK-wide basis.
Scope
Selected two-child policy only. Resolution Foundation models Great Britain, not a full UK or party plan cost; Northern Ireland, the benefit cap and bedroom tax excluded.
Baseline
RF compares abolition with keeping the limit. Benefit take-up may differ in practice. Other benefit changes are excluded.
Year
RF estimate for 2024-25; cash, not a lifetime total. Research published before the election.
Status
2024 election proposal; not current spending or a claim of policy now in force.
Costing
Independent estimate, not a party costing. Resolution Foundation: Abolishing the two-child limit would cost the Government £2.5 billion in 2024-25
Independent assessment
Resolution Foundation: one of the most efficient ways to drive down child poverty rates
Source and dates

Reform UK

Data period: 2024 election manifesto and analysis. Published 2024. Source updated not supplied. Published 2024-06-24. Source updated not supplied.

This is a fixed past snapshot. No next release date is announced.

Selected official offer
Eliminate NHS waiting lists with an annual funding package.
Party source excerpt
NHS Patients will receive a voucher for private treatment if they can’t see a GP within 3 days. For a consultant it would be 3 weeks. For an operation, 9 weeks. Services will always be free at the point of use.
Scope
NHS package and waiting-list target; no geographic split given. IFS disputes the outcome at that cost, not a single staffing measure.
Baseline
Cost of the party's package, not the whole NHS budget. It includes tax relief, patient vouchers and staffing changes; IFS gives no replacement total.
Year
Annualised over a five-year electoral term; no fiscal start year or price basis is stated.
Status
2024 election proposal; not current spending or a claim of policy now in force.
Costing
Party claim: annualised NHS package cost. Party source: NHS PLEDGES COSTS = £17 BILLION PA
Independent assessment
Paul Johnson, IFS: the claim that they could eliminate NHS waiting lists at a cost of £17 billion a year is demonstrably wrong
Source and dates
Party source: PDF page 9; NHS package. Published 2024. Copy saved 2026-11-01. Party publisher. Saved PDF · Plain text. Costing: PDF page 9; NHS package cost. Published 2024. Copy saved 2026-11-01.
